treatments.summary: Early blight is a common fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. It affects leaves, stems, and fruits, reducing yield and quality.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves
cultural_controls: Remove and destroy infected plant debris
Space plants properly for air circulation
Apply mulch to prevent soil splash
Stake plants to keep foliage off ground
biological_controls: Use compost tea to boost plant immunity
chemical_controls: Follow 7-14 day spray intervals during wet weather
prevention: Remove lower leaves as plants grow

treatments.summary: Late blight is a devastating disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. It can destroy entire crops within days under favorable conditions.
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves and stems
Gray-white fuzzy growth on leaf undersides
Brown to black lesions spreading rapidly
Entire plant collapse in severe cases
cultural_controls: Destroy all plant debris after harvest
Water at base of plants only
Remove volunteer tomato and potato plants
biological_controls: Focus on prevention and cultural practices
chemical_controls: Alternate fungicide types to prevent resistance
prevention: Start preventive sprays before disease appears

treatments.summary: Early blight affects potato foliage and tubers, caused by Alternaria solani. It reduces plant vigor and tuber quality.
symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on leaves
Yellowing and dying of lower leaves first
cultural_controls: Hill soil around plants to cover tubers
biological_controls: Incorporate compost to improve soil health
chemical_controls: Start applications when plants are 6 inches tall

treatments.summary: Late blight is the most destructive potato disease, caused by Phytophthora infestans. It was responsible for the Irish potato famine.
symptoms: White fuzzy growth on leaf undersides
cultural_controls: Hill plants high to protect tubers
Harvest only when vines are dead
Avoid irrigation during cool, wet weather
biological_controls: Use as part of integrated approach
chemical_controls: Spray preventively every 5-7 days in wet weather
prevention: Scout fields twice weekly in wet weather

treatments.summary: Apple scab is a serious fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis, affecting leaves, fruits, and sometimes young twigs.
symptoms: Olive-green to brown spots on leaves
cultural_controls: Maintain tree vigor with proper nutrition
biological_controls: Apply beneficial fungi to decompose fallen leaves

treatments.summary: Black rot is a fungal disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa, affecting fruit, leaves, and limbs of apple trees.
symptoms: Purple spots on leaves with light centers
Rotted areas on fruit starting at calyx
Black, circular, sunken lesions on fruit
cultural_controls: Remove mummified fruits from tree and ground
Prune out dead and diseased wood
Remove cankers by pruning below infection
biological_controls: Focus on sanitation and cultural practices
chemical_controls: Spray from pink bud through summer
prevention: Avoid tree stress through proper care

treatments.summary: Black rot is a devastating fungal disease of grapes caused by Guignardia bidwellii, affecting all green parts of the vine.
symptoms: Black pycnidia (fruiting bodies) in leaf spots
Brown lesions on shoots and tendrils
Light brown spots on young berries
Berries shrivel into hard black mummies
Total crop loss in severe cases
biological_controls: Limited effectiveness, use with other methods
chemical_controls: Spray every 10-14 days in wet weather

treatments.summary: Common rust is a fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi, producing rust-colored pustules on corn leaves.
symptoms: Small circular to elongated rust-colored pustules
Pustules turn dark brown or black as season progresses
Severe infections cause premature leaf death
cultural_controls: Plant early to avoid peak rust periods
chemical_controls: Treat only if rust appears before silking
Usually economical only for seed production
prevention: Choose adapted varieties for your region

treatments.summary: Northern leaf blight is a fungal disease caused by Exserohilum turcicum, creating long, elliptical lesions on corn leaves.
symptoms: Long gray-green to tan lesions on leaves
Lesions may merge, destroying entire leaves
Disease progresses from lower to upper leaves
biological_controls: Use as part of integrated approach
chemical_controls: Apply fungicides if disease severe before tasseling
prevention: Choose appropriate hybrids for your area
Monitor fields from V8 growth stage
Avoid continuous corn in same field

treatments.summary: No disease detected. Plant appears healthy with no visible symptoms of disease.
symptoms: No signs of wilting or stress
prevention: Ensure proper spacing and air circulation
